prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: extract_field_from_www_auth() in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py parsed WWW-Authenticate header auth-params with logic that could match on substrings/incomplete tokens instead of properly tokenizing comma-separated auth-params while respecting quoted-string commas — both PRs replace that with a manual, quote-aware comma-splitting parser. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma tokenizer for the WWW-Authenticate header, but #3041 goes further: _extract_bearer_auth_params() splits the *entire* header into per-challenge segments and then scopes param collection to the segment whose scheme token is 'bearer', so headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y, error=z') are handled correctly. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params() only strips text before the first space and flattens everything after it into one param list, so it can't distinguish a second scheme's params from the target challenge's params in a multi-challenge header. #3041's approach is the more complete fix for the same parsing bug.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma tokenizer for the WWW-Authenticate header, but #3041 goes further: _extract_bearer_auth_params() splits the *entire* header into per-challenge segments and then scopes param collection to the segment whose scheme token is 'bearer', so headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y, error=z') are handled correctly. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params() only strips text before the first space and flattens everything after it into one param list, so it can't distinguish a second scheme's params from the target challenge's params in a multi-challenge header. #3041's approach is the more complete fix for the same parsing bug.

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the exact same branch in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) handling the case where a previous assistant tool_use is not followed by a tool_result — but they implement opposite fixes. #2962 makes this case NOT raise (per SEP-1577, a tool_use need not be followed by a tool_result), gating the ID-mismatch check on has_tool_results. #3053 keeps the raise but replaces the generic 'ids do not match' error with an explicit 'tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks' message — i.e. it still treats missing tool_result as invalid. clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma tokenizer for the WWW-Authenticate header, but #3041 goes further: _extract_bearer_auth_params() splits the *entire* header into per-challenge segments and then scopes param collection to the segment whose scheme token is 'bearer', so headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y, error=z') are handled correctly. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params() only strips text before the first space and flattens everything after it into one param list, so it can't distinguish a second scheme's params from the target challenge's params in a multi-challenge header. #3041's approach is the more complete fix for the same parsing bug.
